findings.title: `float: right` on button is ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` now sets `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()` at line 264), which makes `float` a no-op on its children. The `button { float: right; }` rule inside `.small-action` therefore no longer pushes the action button to the right edge; it will be laid out inline right after `.small-action-desc`. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead. To keep the button right-aligned the desc should get `flex: 1` (or the button `margin-left: auto`) instead of relying on floats.

findings.title: Percentage padding on a flex item replaces the fixed offset that cleared the avatar
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` padding changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`. The old left padding of 4em reserved space for the floated 45px avatar; the new value is a percentage of the flex container's width, so on narrow containers the gap between avatar and text collapses to a couple of pixels, and on wide ones it grows arbitrarily. A fixed-length padding/margin (or `flex` sizing) would give stable spacing.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits legacy properties that reject modern values and omits -moz-box-align
findings.body: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` forwards the standard value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy specs only accept `start|end|center|baseline|stretch`. Any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will emit invalid declarations for the old box model / IE10, silently falling back to the default alignment. It also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property, while omitting `-moz-box-align` even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for old Gecko — so in exactly the engine the prefix was added for, alignment is never applied. Either map the values (`flex-start` -> `start`, etc.) or drop the legacy prefixes.

findings.title: order mixin does not translate to the 1-based legacy box-ordinal-group
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1), whereas standard `order` is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same number to both means `@include order(0)` produces an invalid ordinal group, and siblings without an explicit order default to group 1 in the legacy model but 0 in the standard one, so the relative ordering can differ between old prefixed engines and modern ones. The mixin should offset the legacy value (e.g. `$val + 1`) or omit the legacy box prefixes.

findings.title: Header panel right-alignment has no fallback for the legacy box model the mixin claims to support
findings.body: `.panel` lost `float: right` and now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. Auto margins are not honoured by the old `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` model that `flexbox()` explicitly emits, so in those engines the panel (user menu, search, hamburger icons) will sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge, with no float fallback remaining. Either drop the legacy `display` prefixes or keep a fallback alignment.

findings.title: `.valign-helper` rule is dead code after the flex conversion
findings.body: `.valign-helper` relies on `height: 100%` plus `vertical-align: middle` to vertically centre header content. Now that `.contents` is a flex container with `align-items: center`, `vertical-align` has no effect on its children and `height: 100%` resolves against an auto-height flex line, so this rule no longer does anything and should be removed to avoid confusion.
